what_this_is: The D3+D6 adjudication record: buckets 3 (OC green, ET-CC red) and 6 (red in both), each CLOSED over an empty view. Checked, and zero: the record states the question, the measured answer, the mechanism of the emptiness, what an excluded test counts as, what would fill each bucket, and for bucket 6 the asymmetry against the red OC checks. It is normative; Confluence pages 277774465 (bucket 3) and 277741669 (bucket 6) mirror it. Each section echoes its view's count, emptiness_reason and universe under `emptiness`, which G32 holds for equality (MES-144 C1), so a re-projected view that gains a row, or whose premise moves, refuses. It adjudicates no row: there are none.
provenance: [authored 30052, 30053, 30054 | ratified 30055]; brief: the MES-144 body; epic MES-96 rulings bind (PO ruling 29609).

excluded_tests.why: An excluded test is outside ET-CC (A2): none of the tagged tests is a register row, so none is an ET-CC member, so none keys a crosswalk cell, and buckets 3 and 6 are sets of cells. Whether it ran or not moves no cell. Separately, and unchanged: a gate-5 run that reports excluded tests is not a complete gate 5, and the run above excluded none.

fill_conditions.bucket_3: an edge whose OC check is green and whose ET-CC member is red: a stricter ET assertion going red while OC stays green.
fill_conditions.bucket_6: an edge whose OC check and ET-CC member are both red: for example a unit landed against behaviour not yet fixed, red on arrival.
fill_conditions.on_main: UNREACHABLE while DoD gate 5 requires 0 failures: a red ET-CC member cannot merge, so no committed crosswalk can carry a red et verdict that a run confirms. A member here is therefore never a regression on main. It can appear (a) in a crosswalk regenerated on a branch mid-remediation, before the unit is updated; (b) where a stored et_verdict is wrong, which bucket_3_6_controls.exs catches by joining a live run; or (c) under a future ruling that admits known-red members. Route (c) does not exist today.
fill_conditions.superseded_stub_sentence: The stubs said bucket 6 fills as Sprint 7 lands tests from bucket 2a, red on arrival by design. Under gate 5 such a test cannot land red, so that route is unavailable as written (ratification 30055, Q4). Raised for the PO register (Q7), not acted on here.

what_moves_rows_when_remediation_lands.what: the A3 findings routed by the D1 records: edges added for ET-green members
what_moves_rows_when_remediation_lands.moves: By shape, as A3 §3 decides it (MCP.Conformance.MatchKey.bucket/1, conformance/lib/mcp/conformance/match_key.ex; the escalations at crosswalk.ex:57): an edge onto a red check lands in 4a if it is contradicting, in 4b if it is partial, and escalates as divergent_despite_agreement, in no bucket, if it is full; an edge onto a green check lands in 5, or escalates as inconsistent_verdict_pair if it is contradicting. The shape is fixed by A3 when it builds the edge, so a recorded verdict bounds the landing without deciding it: a counterpart recorded as contradicting a red check lands in 4a, and one recorded as agreeing with a red check lands in 4b or escalates, and cannot land in 4a. The classification below enumerates the routed counterparts by that rule. It supersedes this entry's earlier sentence, "An edge onto a red check (RequestMetaInvalid, HttpServerMetaInvalid400) lands in 4a", which was false for the agreeing counterpart it names (CR 30063, B1). Nothing lands in 3 or 6. Both need a red ET verdict, and the members are ET-green: mechanism.criterion_run.

classification.population: every row, in every record of docs/conformance/adjudications/, whose routed_to.owner is MES-152; per row, its oc_counterpart (the primary counterpart) and, separately, each entry of its oc_counterpart.also (the secondary counterparts). A counterpart's check status is its token's status in docs/conformance/in-scope-2026-07-28.json. Re-derived from the D1 records, not copied from the review.
classification.rule: lands = f(check status, recorded verdict): FAILURE and contradicts gives 4a; FAILURE and agrees gives 4b or an escalation (the shape decides); SUCCESS and contradicts gives an escalation; SUCCESS with agrees or with no verdict recorded gives 5. The client-leg records carry no verdict field on the counterpart. None of those rows' counterpart or rationale text says "contradict" (a text measure), so they are classed as not contradicting.

d1_contradicting_units.what: The D1 records of Sprint 13 measured, by mutation of lib/, ET-CC units that contradict red OC checks, mostly through request construction: the member's own request, built by a test helper, carries an incomplete _meta, and M9 (a -32602 gate on a request whose _meta is incomplete, what RequestMetaInvalid requires) turns the member red. The bucket-1 members listed below pass today and go red under M9. Read from the merged records' mutations; not re-adjudicated here. The records' dispositions for them are in disposition_split: all but one are redundant, and one is wrong_against_spec.
d1_contradicting_units.note: The union is taken over tags. The slices are disjoint, so it is also their sum. M9h and M9f figures are quoted per record, not summed: they were not measured on MES-141's slice.

construction_wording.what: The M9_union rows whose own record text says, in terms, that the contradiction is "only through the construction". A text measure, not a re-reading: the rows outside this list do not use the phrase, and whether their contradiction also runs through construction is not re-adjudicated here.

asymmetry_bucket_6.what_it_implies: The suite is not independent of the implementation. Where lib/ diverges from the specification, ET-CC does not detect the divergence: it encodes it as a green assertion. So red OC checks sit against zero red ET members, and the contradicting units are green by construction. Bucket 6 being empty is evidence of that coupling, not evidence of agreement.

census_negative.what: The in-scope predicate above is the ratified one (ratification 30055, Q6). The stub's literal predicate, the census's scored FAILURE total per leg, gives a different client figure, and the difference is named here so that the client figure of by_leg is not read as a census figure.
census_negative.reading: Every scored client FAILURE sits in a scenario classified out_of_scope_adr_003 (the authorization profile, excluded from 2.0.0 by ADR-003), which the in-scope set does not carry. So by the in-scope predicate the client leg contributes no failing check, and by the census's scored totals it contributes the ADR-003 ones. The server figure is the same under both.
